label: Early copy steps (2nd/3rd output) of long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost always on the second output step (input = first copied token, right after <DEL>, recall_idx 1; 82% of mass) or the third (recall_idx 2; 16%), and only when the sequence is long (L >= 7; nothing for L <= 5). The firing probability goes up with the number of outputs still left, L - recall_idx: about 98% at recall_idx 1 with L=9, high at recall_idx 1 with L=8 and at recall_idx 2 with L=9, and about 37-51% where L - recall_idx = 6. The strongest activations are at recall_idx 1 with L=9, with mild modulation by the input token (v, w, s are strongest). It never fires in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on the first output step (recall_idx 0). It is close to silent on later copy steps, apart from a small tail on the last couple of steps of L=9 sequences. In short, it marks positions shortly after <DEL> when many outputs are still to come.

issues: The numbers in the explanation check out. Cell precisions on dev: L9/r1 0.999 (the explanation says ~98%), L8/r1 0.954, L9/r2 0.692, L7/r1 0.511, L8/r2 0.366, L6 under 2%, L<=5 zero. Recall_idx 1 and 2 hold 82% and 16% of activation mass. It never fires in the original phase, on <DEL>, or at recall_idx 0.
The predicate's test F1 is 0.799, below the 0.8 cutoff for 'explained'. So by the stated criterion the verdict should not be 'explained'.

The explanation says the input token shifts the size 'a little'. It does much more than that: in the borderline cells, the current input token decides whether the unit fires at all. At L7/r1, firing rate by input token (= orig(0)) is v 0.99, w 0.92, f/n 0.90, s 0.88, z 0.85, k 0.80, but i 0.01, m 0.06, 2 0.06, t 0.08, h 0.16. At L8/r2 with input orig(1): v 1.00, w 0.96, s 0.88, k 0.84, r 0.82, but i 0.00, 2 0.01, m 0.02, h 0.03, o 0.06. The false positives (14k on test) and misses at L7/r1 and L8/r2 follow this token split. That is a systematic gap, not noise.

Firing at L8/r2 on good tokens is left out of the predicate entirely. These are the systematic misses, along with a small late-step tail (L9, recall_idx >= 6: precision 0.036, mass 0.9%) that is correctly described as minor.
skeptic.revised_label: Second/third copy step of long sequences. Always fires at recall_idx 1 when L >= 8. When fewer outputs remain (L7/r1, L8/r2, L9/r2), it fires only if the current input token is in a favoured set (v, w, s, k, r, b, z, ...) and never on i, m, h, t, 2.
skeptic.better_predicate: ((recall_idx==1)&(L>=8)) | ((recall_idx==1)&(L==7)&isin(in_tok,[tok(c) for c in 'bfknpqrsuvwz1lg'])) | ((recall_idx==2)&(L==9)&~isin(in_tok,[tok(c) for c in 'himt2jyo0'])) | ((recall_idx==2)&(L==8)&isin(in_tok,[tok(c) for c in 'bkrsvwz']))
